content:
The PR #43982 came about when I was porting a recently found, LLM-formalised construction to Redhill (the n=4n=4n=4 case of Ramaekers's conjecture). It simply deprecates sub_lt_zero, which is already an alias of sub_neg.

@Monica Omar spoke out against this saying that sub_neg could be confused for the LHS of sub_neg_eq_add. But I disagree – sub_neg already has a docstring referring to sub_neg_eq_add.
I mean we could deprecate sub_neg_eq_add in favour of sub_neg (a - -b) and sub_lt_zero (a - b < 0) if you prefer shorter names
Yeah, especially because mul_neg and div_neg exist, but are different from add_neg and sub_neg. Why not make them the same?

I think one of the advantages of an alias is to make it easier for the user to find what they want, regardless if it's longer or not. We have plenty of aliases that have longer names, but they are useful to keep around.
